title: Audit stream contracts and evolution notes (2026 Q1)
body:
Purpose
-----
This note collects working ideas for a backward-compatible evolution of our audit event contracts, evidence handoff references, and SIEM export shaping. Goal: make a pragmatic, versioned path from current v1/v2 mixes to a stable v3 export that supports RBAC v2 semantics and forensic-grade evidence linking without breaking downstream SIEM parsers.

Context and constraints
-----------------------
- Many of our producers today emit slightly different envelopes (some include nested `actor` objects, others flatten `actor_id` and `actor_role`).
- Downstream consumers (Splunk, Elastic, internal forensic tooling) assume compact, canonical fields for indexing. Breaking changes are costly.
- Evidence automation requires durable, low-cardinality references (opaque IDs) that can be dereferenced to S3/GS, archived snapshots, or KMS-rewrapped artifacts.
- RBAC v2 introduces richer role and principal metadata (policy_id, role_bindings) that we want to attach to audit frames without exploding event size.

High-level proposal
-------------------
1) Introduce explicit contract_version on every emitted frame: integer (1,2,3...). Producer runtime must add `contract_version`=2 for the transitional rollout.
2) Standardize event_id to ULID (lower collision risk, monotonic) and require event_id in all exports.
3) Use shallow top-level fields for indexing-critical attributes and defer bulk metadata to `evidence_refs` or `attachments` arrays with small object IDs.
4) Evidence handoff -> standardize `evidence_refs` as list of short tokens: <bucket>:<prefix>:<object-id> or presigned URL. Expand with `evidence_manifest_id` when there are many artifacts.
5) RBAC v2 metadata: attach `rbac_snapshot_id` (referenced blob) and `rbac_delta_hint` (small text summary) rather than fully serializing policy documents per event.

Suggested canonical envelope (indexable fields only)
---------------------------------------------------
- contract_version: int
- event_id: string (ULID)
- ts: string (ISO8601 UTC)
- source: string (service name)
- actor_type: string (user|service|machine)
- actor_id: string
- action: string (verb.namespace)
- target_type: string
- target_id: string
- outcome: string (success|failure|error)
- outcome_code: string (optional short code for classification)
- evidence_refs: string[] (comma-separated tokens or array in JSON body)
- rbac_snapshot_id: string (optional)
- tracing_id: string (optional request/trace linkage)

Notes: keep envelope under ~8KB for efficient transport. Anything larger must go to attachments/evidence manifests.

Evidence orchestration and lifecycle
-----------------------------------
- Producers should upload large evidence objects (logs, request bodies, model outputs) to the evidence bucket and emit only references in the event.
- We propose a short-lived presigned model for daily forensic access, plus a long-term archival manifest (read-only) for 7+ years retention for regulated customers.
- Evidence manifests are JSON blobs keyed by `evidence_manifest_id` and contain: list of objects, sha256 digests, content-type, mime hints, and access hints (presigned OR archival path).
- Automation: a small evidence indexer will listen to audit stream, fetch new manifest IDs and validate presence and digests asynchronously. Failures generate an operational alert but do not block event emission.

SIEM export shaping
-------------------
- Export pipeline will map the canonical envelope to SIEM-friendly flattened records. For initial rollout, we will support two export modes: 
  * Minimal (indexable fields only) -> ideal for high-throughput telemetry.
  * Forensic (index + evidence_manifest_id) -> for high-fidelity investigations.
- Backcompat: if contract_version missing, assume legacy v1 flattening and run transform heuristics. We will emit a `transform_hint` header when heuristics applied.

Versioning and migration plan
----------------------------
Phase 0 (now) - experiments
- Ship producer runtime change that adds `contract_version`=2 and `event_id` ULIDs in a non-breaking way. Keep alternate actor encodings for a week.
Phase 1 - adapters
- Introduce translation layer in the stream broker to normalize incoming envelopes to canonical fields for downstream consumers that request it. Disable by default.
Phase 2 - opt-in consumers
- Expose new SIEM export config that can request `contract_version`=2 normalized streams. Encourage Splunk/Elastic teams to validate mapping.
Phase 3 - enforce and prune
- After 60 days of opt-in and monitoring, flip normalization on by default and require producers to emit contract_version. After 6 months, begin deprecating legacy shapes with a 90-day notice.

Compatibility concerns
----------------------
- ULID adoption: need SDKs in Java/Go/Python runtimes. Fallback to UUID4 if ULID not available for older clients but add monotonic component where possible.
- Big attachments: We must avoid sending full policy documents per event. Use snapshots.
- Rate of evidence indexing: forensic indexer must be horizontally scalable and able to backpressure (alerts) rather than block.

Operational checks and telemetry
-------------------------------
- Monitor: percentage of events without `contract_version`; event_id uniqueness collisions (should be ~0); size distribution of envelopes; number of missing evidence manifests within 24h.
- Dashboards: contract adoption by service, evidence_ref per 1000 events, RBAC snapshot attach rate.

Open questions / TODOs
----------------------
- Should we mandate ULID encoding in base62 or base32? (ULID standard is base32)
- How to surface RBAC deltas compactly for quick triage without fetching snapshot? Proposal: `rbac_delta_hint` max 256 bytes.
- Policy for presigned URL TTLs when evidence manifests are referenced from archived exports.
- Concurrency: do we allow multiple evidence_manifest_ids on a single event? Yes, but prefer single manifest to simplify lookups.

Immediate action items (next 2 weeks)
-------------------------------------
- Draft SDK helpers to emit `contract_version` and ULID. (assign: eng-serving-runtime)
- Prototype evidence manifest schema and uploader (assign: infra)
- Create Splunk transform PR for canonical mapping (assign: observability)
- Run simulated ingest test for 100k events/day with sample manifests (assign: SRE)

Appendix: example event (indexable portion only)
------------------------------------------------
{
  contract_version: 2,
  event_id: 01F8MECHZX3TBDSZ7UN3F6N5Y0,
  ts: 2026-01-14T18:22:31Z,
  source: serving-runtime.attention,
  actor_type: user,
  actor_id: u_10293,
  action: model.generate.completion,
  target_type: model,
  target_id: m-gpt-4x,
  outcome: success,
  evidence_refs: ["evi:s3:manifests/2026/01/14/m-gpt-4x-req-01.json"],
  rbac_snapshot_id: rs_20260114_03
}

Notes-to-self style bits (informal)
----------------------------------
- Keep this doc light and actionable. We want concrete artifacts (SDK helpers, transform PRs, prototype indexer) within 2 sprints.
- Expect some pushback from teams that prefer full policy inlined for debugging — counter with small helper that can fetch snapshot quickly.

References and similar work
---------------------------
- event-canonicalization-and-idempotency-playbook (confluence)
- audit-envelope-contract-and-retrofit-guidance-v1p0 (internal doc)

If you have concerns or want to pair on the SIEM mapping, ping me in #sec-audit (slack) or add comments to JIRA-SEC-4821.
